title: Claude chat to Cowork — brainstorm, prototype in chat, then hand off to build
summary: A build workflow for a viral camera-based web project: brainstorm in Claude chat and have it ask questions before building, confirm which tools it will use, demand an interactive prototype in chat, then have Claude write a detailed build prompt and hand it to Claude Cowork, which has terminal and computer access and executes it end to end into a working HTML file.
takeaways: Make Claude ask questions before it writes any code
Get an interactive prototype in chat before committing to a build
Have Claude write the build prompt, then run it in an agent with system access

title: PLFM_RADAR — open-source radar with PCBs, FPGA code and Python GUI
summary: github.com/NawfalMotii79/PLFM_RADAR is an MIT-licensed radar project shipping complete PCBs, FPGA code, full schematics and a Python GUI, claimed to track multiple targets out to 20 km. The "military-grade" and "$250K" lines are hype, and a commenter rightly warns to read unknown repos before running anything from them.
takeaways: Rare full-stack open radar: boards, gateware and GUI in one repo
Treat the 20 km range claim as unverified until you read the design
Audit any repo pushed by hype reels before running binaries

title: Identity-preserving portrait prompt — Sony A1 85mm editorial re-render
summary: A reusable image-edit prompt that enhances a portrait while locking identity, facial geometry, expression and background. It forces a camera spec (Sony A1, 85mm f/1.4 at f/1.6, ISO 100, 1/200), matches the reference lighting direction, and asks for real skin texture, film grain, 10-bit 4K and no plastic smoothing. The post does not say which image model it was run on.
takeaways: Name a concrete camera and lens to anchor realism
Explicitly forbid background, layout and face-shape changes
Ask for skin texture and grain to avoid the plastic AI look

title: Everything is a mass on a spring — the harmonic oscillator everywhere
summary: A quick physics riff: LC circuits, electron and molecular vibrations, optical tweezers and even quantum field theory all reduce to the simple harmonic oscillator. Fun reminder of why that one model is worth learning cold; the caption plugs an algebra guide.
takeaways: Learn the mass-on-a-spring model deeply; it transfers across physics
LC circuits and molecular vibrations share the same math

title: Claude resume prompts — ATS diagnosis, keyword gaps, XYZ rewrite, mock interview

takeaways: Rewrite bullets as accomplished X, measured by Y, by doing Z
Use Claude as a hiring manager for scored mock interviews
Compare your resume to real job posts to find missing keywords

title: Artist statement in four sentences — what, why, how, and the takeaway
summary: A tight template: sentence one says what you make in plain English ("I make large oil paintings of empty rooms"), two says why this subject and nothing else, three names only the process that changes the meaning, and four states what you want viewers to take away. Cut the copied art-speak. The creator also sells a book with templates.
takeaways: If a stranger cannot picture the work from sentence one, rewrite it
Mention process only when it changes what the work says
The why sentence is the one collectors remember

title: Scott Pelley on press freedom — "there is no democracy without journalism"
summary: A clip from Scott Pelley's New York Times interview with Lulu Garcia-Navarro, responding to Trump calling him a stiff who doesn't care about the country. He cites covering combat in Iraq, Afghanistan and Kuwait and argues a free press is required for an informed public. Commentary, not analysis.
takeaways: Judge reporting by facts, not by whether you like the messenger

title: Artist housing matcher — placing artists in empty NYC pied-à-terres
summary: @madisonteresaaa built a website that matches artists with wealthy owners of New York pied-à-terres, so owners can avoid a proposed vacancy tax while gaining cultural cachet, framed as Medici-style patronage. A provocative two-sided marketplace idea, with comments arguing it helps the rich dodge taxes.
takeaways: Policy changes create matchmaking opportunities
Expect pushback when a product helps owners avoid a tax
